title: Max Verstappen calls those enjoying new F1 racing style ‘not real’ fans
content:
Max Verstappen has launched another stinging broadside against the new style of Formula 1 racing being produced by its new cars and engines, calling those that enjoy the spectacle witnessed early in the 2026 season “not real” fans.

The Dutchman endured a difficult weekend at the Chinese Grand Prix, which was won by Kimi Antonelli ahead of George Russell — giving Mercedes another 1-2 result at the start of F1’s new rules era.

Verstappen could only finish ninth in Saturday’s sprint race and then retired from Sunday’s main race due to a cooling problem on his engine’s electrical energy recovery system. He also struggled throughout both qualifying sessions as he struggled with the handling of his Red Bull car.

Afterwards, the four-time world champion said it was “a very bad weekend” for Red Bull, before he was asked again for his thoughts on F1’s new style of racing.

The Chinese race followed last Sunday’s Australia season opener in featuring many “yo-yo” style passes — a phrase coined by 2025 world Lando Norris, to describe how drivers can now get by a rival using more electrical engine energy, before being quickly repassed in turn shortly afterwards when that energy wanes.

Verstappen called this “anti-racing” and “not a lot of fun” during preseason testing.

“It’s (still) terrible,” Verstappen replied when asked by reporters post-race on Sunday if the racing had been “less artificial” in China compared the action in Australia.

“If someone likes this, then you really don’t know what racing is about. It’s not fun at all. It’s playing Mario Kart. This is not racing.

He added: “You are boosting past, then you run out of battery the next straight, they boost past you again. For me, it’s just a joke.”

Double world champion and Aston Martin driver Fernando Alonso, meanwhile, called the 2026 F1 season “this battery world championship.” Aston’s car is currently being held back with a severe vibration engine issue that is breaking its batteries

There is currently a split in driver opinion that can be divided along those that are achieving positive results early in the new rules era and those that are not.

After finishing third in Sunday’s Chinese GP — and claiming his first Ferrari podium — Lewis Hamilton said it was “the best racing that I’ve ever experienced in Formula 1,” referring to how the narrower and shorter cars can follow each other more easily compared to the cars used in 2025, alongside the battery deployment racing style.

Mercedes team boss Toto Wolff said “I think the product is good in itself,” in the aftermath of Antonelli’s win.

Verstappen, though, said he would have the same opinion if he were winning races

“It’s not about being upset of where I am,” he said. “Because I’m actually fighting even more now (compared to 2023, when he won 19 out of 22 races).

“You get to understand what (racing) is about even more (down the order). For me, it’s really a joke.”

The Dutchman has had reservations about the new engines as far back as 2023, when they were first tested on simulators at the factories of the manufacturer squads.

At the time, Red Bull complaints, which included concerns from former team principal Christian Horner, where treated by many people in the F1 paddock as politicking aimed at preserving its position at the front of the pack. It then lost this in any case when McLaren surged in 2024 and 2025.

The F1 organization and motorsport governing body, the FIA, have been closely monitoring discussion on the new cars.

It remains possible there will be changes to the engine rules, which could reduce the amount of electrical engine power and increase that coming from the internal combustion element.

This would at least reduce the amount the cars need to be held back in high-speed corners and at the end of straights to recharge the batteries, as they do now.

“We are talking about it,” Verstappen said of these discussions. “I think they understand where we are coming from as the drivers. I think I speak for most of the drivers. Some, of course, will say it’s great because they are winning races, which is fair enough. When you have an advantage, why would you give that up?

“Because you never know if you’re going to have a good car again. But if you just speak to most of the drivers, it’s not what we like. I don’t think it’s what the real F1 fans like.

“Maybe some fans like it, but they don’t understand racing. Hopefully we can get rid of this as soon as possible.

Verstappen also predicted that if F1 prioritizes the style of racing he does not like, “it will come and bite them back in the ass” and “eventually ruin the sport”, if fans that enjoyed racing in previous F1 eras become alienated by the new spectacle.
